sentences.text:
Opponents No.1 to 3 i.e.
owner and insurance company of the Car NO.GJ-03-DN-3129 and owner of the Motorcycle No.GJ-03-BR-2277 liable, jointly and several.
2. Brief facts of the case, as per claimant/s, are as under :
2.1

That on 24.12.2014 at abou 12:00 noon, when deceased - Aditya Rajendrabhai Antala was going as pillion rider on Motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ-03-BR-2277 and when he reached near the place of accident i.e. Opp.
R.K. Park, Airport Road, Rajkot, the driver of the Car bearing registration No.GJ-03-DN-3129 came from opposite side with full speed and in negligent manner and by coming on the wrong side, hit the motorcycle of the deceased.

As a result, the deceased sustained serious injuries and ultimately,
deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3735/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined

the legal heirs of the deceased - parents and younger brother have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.20 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent No.1 i.e. owner of the Car has chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.

Opponents No.2 and 3 i.e. insurance company of the car and owner of the motorcycle have appeared and filed their written statements / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimants in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the appellant - insurance company for exoneration.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Palak Thakkar for the appellant - insurance company of the Car (original opponent No.2) has raised only one contention before this Court that the driver-cum-owner of the case was not holding valid driving license at all on the date of accident, as the accident has occurred on 24.12.2014 and the validity of the license was for the period from 10.11.2004 to 20.11.2012.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has ordered pay and recover, which cannot be passed as there was not only violation of condition of insurance policy but also of the provisions of the Act.
He has submitted that the appellant - insurance company may be exonerated.
He has submitted that the award may be modified and this appeal may be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Tushar Sheth for the original claimants has submitted that the driver was holding driving license for the period from 10.011.2004 to 20.11.2012 and it was not renewed at the time accident.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the driver was not knowing driving.
He has submitted that it is a case of composite negligence.
The deceased was a pillion rider.
The Tribunal has held 90% negligence on the part of the car driver and 10% negligence on the part of the motorcycle driver.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly passed an order of pay and recover.
He has submitted that the impugned order is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3735/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined just and proper and no interference be made by this Court.
He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
6.1 From the record, it transpires that the accident NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3735/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined has occurred between the car and the motorcycle.
The deceased was a pillion rider.
The Tribunal has held 90% negligence on the part of the car driver and 10% negligence on the part of the motorcycle driver.

Further, from the deposition of the witness i.e.
RTO Officer, it has not come on record that the driver was disqualified to driver the vehicle in question.
Further, it is a matter of record that the driver was holding driving license for the period from 10.011.2004 to 20.11.2012.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the driver was not knowing driving that too merely on presumption about absence of renewal of driving license.
Further, it was not on record that the license was issued by any other RTO except Rajkot.
Therefore, the insurance company has failed to prove the said fact before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, the Tribunal has rightly passed an order of pay and recover.
The impugned judgment and award is just and proper and this Court does not warrant any interference.
This appeal therefore needs to be dismissed.
7. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
7.1 The present appeal is hereby dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3735/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 7.2

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire awarded amount, if yet not deposited, with interest and cost as decided by the Tribunal, from the date of claim petition till its realisation, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
It would be open for the appellant - insurance company to recover the proportionate amount, as apportioned by the Tribunal, from the other tort- feasors, in accordance with law.

7.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal (including enhanced amount), with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the respective claimant/s, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
7.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the court fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
7.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
